claim.claim-text: 1. An aircraft (10) defining a longitudinal direction and comprising:

a fuselage (12) extending between a forward end (16) and an aft end (18) along the longitudinal direction of the aircraft (10); an aft engine mounted to the aft end (18) of the fuselage (12), the aft engine further comprising a nacelle (306) including a forward section (330); and an airflow duct (344) extending at least partially through the nacelle (306) of the aft engine and defining an outlet (346) on the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306) for providing an airflow to the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306), wherein the airflow duct (344) includes a plurality of outlets (246), the plurality of outlets (246) including at least one first outlet (346) positioned outward of a baseline stagnation point (340) of a bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306) and at least one second outlet (346) positioned inward of the baseline stagnation point (340) of the bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306).

2. The aircraft (10) of claim 1, wherein airflow is directed through the at least one first outlet (346) positioned outward of a baseline stagnation point (340) and the at least one second outlet (346) positioned inward of the baseline stagnation point (340) simultaneously.
3. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306) defines a lip, and wherein the outlet (346) is positioned on the lip.

4. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the plurality of outlets (246) are spaced along a bottom lip (338) of a bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306), and wherein the plurality of outlets (246) are proximate a bottom-most point of the bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306).

5. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the nacelle (306) defines an inner surface (354), and wherein the airflow duct (344) defines an inlet (348) on the inner surface (354) of the nacelle (306).

6. The aircraft (10) of claim 4 or 5, wherein the aft engine comprises a fan (304), and wherein the airflow duct (344) defines an inlet (348) on an inner surface (354) of the nacelle (306) downstream from the fan (304).

7. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the aft engine comprises a support member extending from the fuselage (12) of the aircraft (10) to the nacelle (306), and wherein the airflow duct (344) extends at least partially through the support member.
8. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, wherein the airflow duct (344) is configured to receive an airflow from a location remote from the aft engine.

9. The aircraft (10) of claim 8, wherein the airflow duct (344) extends at least partially through the nacelle (306), through one or more structural members and forward through the fuselage (12) of the aircraft (10).
10. The aircraft (10) of claim 9, wherein the one or more of the structural members are positioned upstream of at least one blade.
11. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, further comprising: a variable throughput valve (356) positioned at least partially within the airflow duct (344).

12. The aircraft (10) of any one of the preceding claims, further comprising: a pair of wings (20) and a pair of aircraft (10) engines (104, 106), each aircraft (10) engine being mounted to a respective one of the pair of wings (20).

13. A method for operating an aircraft (10) defining a longitudinal direction, the aircraft (10) including a fuselage (12) extending between a forward end (16) and an aft end (18) along the longitudinal direction of the aircraft (10), a pair of wings (20), and a pair of aircraft (10) engines (104, 106), each aircraft (10) engine (104, 106) being mounted to a respective one of the pair of wings (20), each aircraft (10) engine (104, 106) further comprising a nacelle (306) including a forward section (330), the method comprising:

directing an airflow through an airflow duct (344) extending at least partially through the nacelle (306) of one or both of the aircraft (10) engines (104, 106), wherein each aircraft (10) engine (104, 106) defines an outlet (346) on the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306) for providing an airflow to the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306), and wherein the airflow duct (344) includes a plurality of outlets (246), the plurality of outlets (246) including at least one first outlet (346) positioned outward of a baseline stagnation point (340) of a bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306) and at least one second outlet (346) positioned inward of the baseline stagnation point (340) of the bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306).

14. The method of claim 13, wherein airflow is directed through the at least one first outlet (346) positioned outward of a baseline stagnation point (340) and the at least one second outlet (346) positioned inward of the baseline stagnation point (340) simultaneously.

15. The method of claim 13 or 14, wherein the plurality of outlets (246) are spaced along a bottom lip (338) of a bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306), and wherein the plurality of outlets (246) are proximate a bottom-most point of the bottom portion (334) of the forward section (330) of the nacelle (306).
